"'''Unwell'''" is a song by American [[alternative rock]] group [[Matchbox Twenty]]. Released on February 3, 2003, as the second single from their third album, ''[[More Than You Think You Are]]'' (2002), it was written by Matchbox Twenty lead singer [[Rob Thomas (musician)|Rob Thomas]]. "Unwell" spent 18 weeks atop the US ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Adult Top 40]] chart and two weeks atop the ''Billboard'' [[Adult Contemporary (chart)|Adult Contemporary]] chart. It also reached {{abbr|No.|Number}} 5 on the ''Billboard'' [[Hot 100]], becoming their third and final top-10 hit. Internationally, the single became a top-20 hit in Australia, peaking at No. 12, and a top-10 hit in New Zealand, peaking at No. 8. "Unwell" was nominated for a [[Grammy Award]] in 2004 for [[Grammy Award for Best Pop Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals|Best Pop Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocal]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sns-grammys-nominees-story.html|title=Complete list of 46th annual Grammy winners and nominees|agency=[[Associated Press]]|website=[[Chicago Tribune]]|date=December 4, 2003|access-date=November 30, 2020}}</ref>

"Unwell" is a song by American alternative rock group Matchbox Twenty. Released on February 3, 2003, as the second single from their third album, More Than You Think You Are (2002), it was written by Matchbox Twenty lead singer Rob Thomas. "Unwell" spent 18 weeks atop the US Billboard Adult Top 40 chart and two weeks atop the Billboard Adult Contemporary chart. It also reached {{abbr|No.|Number}} 5 on the Billboard Hot 100, becoming their third and final top-10 hit. Internationally, the single became a top-20 hit in Australia, peaking at No. 12, and a top-10 hit in New Zealand, peaking at No. 8. "Unwell" was nominated for a Grammy Award in 2004 for Best Pop Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocal.

sections.heading: Content
sections.wikitext: On the live DVD ''Show: A Night in the Life of Matchbox Twenty'', lead singer [[Rob Thomas (musician)|Rob Thomas]] states that he wrote the song as a metaphor for humanity in general, a song for people who are "messed up and feel alone like that. We all feel a little messed up sometimes... you're not alone."
sections.text: On the live DVD Show: A Night in the Life of Matchbox Twenty, lead singer Rob Thomas states that he wrote the song as a metaphor for humanity in general, a song for people who are "messed up and feel alone like that. We all feel a little messed up sometimes... you're not alone."

sections.heading: Reception
sections.wikitext: The song was the second most-played song in the United States in 2003 according to ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' magazine. The music video was No. 1 on [[VH1]]'s Top 40 Videos of 2003. In 2011, VH1 named the song as the 82nd best song of the 2000s.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext: Directed by [[Meiert Avis]], the music video predominantly features Thomas seeing various odd occurrences throughout, all the while singing along to the song. The other band members only appear in cameos, notably when Thomas boards a subway and they are seen in the background. The appearance of the other bandmates is also altered like most of the video (their noses are rather large). The other band members are also seen at the end of the video gathered in Thomas' room, and each takes their turn waving goodbye to the camera before Thomas does so as well at the end of the video. One of the reasons Thomas picked Avis to direct is because his concept for the video was the closest thing to an acid trip out of every other idea.
